newsitem.title: CROATIA: Supreme court confirms Bosnian Croat's extradition.
newsitem.headline: Supreme court confirms Bosnian Croat's extradition.

text.p: The Croatian Supreme Court confirmed on Thursday that the extradition of a Bosnian Croat indicted by the U.N. War Crimes Tribunal in The Hague could go ahead, the state news agency HINA reported.
The court ruled that Zlatko Aleksovski would be sent to The Hague unless the justice minister postponed the extradition for "well-founded" reasons, HINA said.
Aleksovski, one of six Bosnian Croats charged with crimes related to ethnic cleansing of Moslems in Bosnia's central Lasva valley in 1993, was arrested in June in Split.
His extradition would be the first time a judicial authority had used a recently passed law on cooperation with the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia (ICTY).

In July a local county court ruled that it would comply with the tribunal's reqeuest to turn Aleksovski over. But his lawyers called on the Supreme Court to annul the ruling, citing health and family reasons.
The Hague Tribunal has so far indicted more than 70 Bosnian Serbs, Croats and Moslems, but only a few have been arrested. The majority are still at large.
Zagreb has been under growing Western pressure to surrender indicted Bosnian Croats, some of whom are believed to be living in Croatia.
Bosnian Croat general Tihomir Blaskic handed himself over volutarily to The Hague in April.
